correctness.rationale: In an SPD matrix of order at most three, the only possible nontrivial natural-order IC(0) dropped fill is position (3,2) when a23=0 and a12,a13≠0. The IC(0) last pivot then equals a33−a13²/a11>0 by the {1,3} principal minor. The displayed four-cycle A(t)=I+tB has B²=2I, so is SPD exactly 0≤t<1/√2. Its IC(0) squared pivots are 1, 1−t², (1−2t²)/(1−t²), (1−t²)(1−3t²)/(1−2t²); within the SPD interval the last is zero at t=1/√3 and negative thereafter. The critical family condition number is (1+√(2/3))/(1−√(2/3))=5+2√6. Kershaw historical witness is 3A(2/3), with pivots (3,5/3,3/5,−5). New independent symbolic factorization verified all identities and the rational witness. Claims are strictly for exact unshifted IC(0), natural order and the displayed family-specific κ, not a global SPD condition threshold.

value.rationale: IC(0) breakdown on SPD systems is a practical question motivating shifts and robust preconditioners. The minimal dimension and sharp continuous onset in the signed cycle containing the classical matrix answer a natural robustness question that one isolated witness does not: they quantify how an SPD margin and pivot margin separate. The κ constant is explicitly restricted to the Jacobi-scaled family, not inflated to an unsupported universal bound.
